intro.text:
The Ahmed body is a simplified car shape used to study aerodynamic drag.

This is a slice through its centre plane.

outro.text:
In wind tunnels the slope flow partly reattaches. Steady RANS models like this one often miss that.

captions.text: A 1.04 m car-like body at 40 m/s (144 km/h), 5 cm above a moving road. White lines are streamlines.
At the rounded nose the air is brought to a stop. This stagnation point has the highest pressure.
Squeezed through the 5 cm gap underneath, the air speeds up to nearly 50 m/s.
Over the 25° rear slope the flow breaks away from the surface.
Close to the slope the air runs backwards, up the slope, at up to 15 m/s. Behind the flat back it swirls in a wake about 25 cm long.
Low pressure on the slope and the flat back pulls the body backwards. That is most of its drag.
Drag coefficient: 0.290 here, 0.285 measured in the wind tunnel (Ahmed, 1984).
